rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God charged Moses here with two tasks: bring his people from unbelief to faith and remind them of God's days.
rows.anchor: أمر موسى عليه السلام في هذا المقام بشيئين : أحدهما : أن يخرجهم من ظلمات الكفر ، والثاني : أن يذكرهم بأيام الله

rows.speaker: الواحدي
rows.claim: Al-Wāḥidī defines yawm as the interval from sunrise to sunset and derives ayyām from aywām, with yāʾ prevailing in assimilation.
rows.anchor: قال الواحدي : أيام جمع يوم ، واليوم هو مقدار المدة من طلوع الشمس إلى غروبها ، وكانت الأيام في الأصل أيوام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Days can stand for momentous events, as in the Arab-days idiom and proverb about one day's joy at another's defeat becoming grief at one's own; 3:140 uses the same idiom.
rows.anchor: يعبر بالأيام عن الوقائع العظيمة التي وقعت فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reminding Israel of God's days means exhorting them through promise and encouragement for past believers' blessings, and warning of punishment for nations such as ʿĀd and Thamūd who rejected messengers.
rows.anchor: عظهم بالترغيب والترهيب والوعد والوعيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses' days of God included Israel's tribulation under Pharaoh and days of ease through manna and quails, the sea's parting, and cloud shade.
rows.anchor: منها ما كان أيام المحنة والبلاء وهي الأيام التي كانت بنو إسرائيل فيها تحت قهر فرعون ومنها ما كان أيام الراحة والنعماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The patient meet hardship with patience and the grateful meet blessings with gratitude; a believer should always be occupied by one of these two responses.
rows.anchor: فإن كان الأول ، كان المؤمن صبارا ، وإن كان الثاني كان شكورا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One answer says the reminders are effectively signs only for the patient and grateful because they are the ones who benefit, as with guidance for the God-fearing and warning for those who fear it.
rows.anchor: لما كانوا هم المنتفعون بتلك الآيات صارت كأنها ليست آيات إلا لهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second answer is that only someone patient or grateful can benefit from this kind of reminder; others gain nothing from the signs.
rows.anchor: الانتفاع بهذا النوع من التذكير لا يمكن حصوله إلا لمن كان صابرا أو شاكرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In “when He rescued you,” the temporal clause qualifies niʿma, understood as God's act of bestowing a favor.
rows.anchor: فقوله : { إذ أنجاكم } ظرف للنعمة بمعنى الأنعام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In 2:49, “they slaughtered” without conjunction explains the evil torment; here the waw makes slaughter an additional kind of torment alongside the other abuse.
rows.anchor: في سورة البقرة : { يذبحون } بغير واو لأنه تفسير لقوله : { سوء العذاب }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation calls Pharaoh's family's acts a divine trial because God enabled them to commit those acts against Israel.
rows.anchor: أن تمكين الله إياهم حتى فعلوا ما فعلوا كان بلاء من الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī prefers that “trial” refers to Israel's rescue: a trial can be hardship or blessing, and this reading fits the verse's opening remembrance of God's favor; 21:35 says both are tests.
rows.anchor: وهو أن ذلك إشارة إلى الإنجاء ، وهو بلاء عظيم ، والبلاء هو الابتلاء ، وذلك قد يكون بالنعمة تارة ، وبالمحنة أخرى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Iblīs excludes God's sincere servants because he knows his scheming will not work on them and they will not accept it.
rows.anchor: اعلم أن إبليس استثنى المخلصين ، لأنه علم أن كيده لا يعمل فيهم ، ولا يقبلون منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī recalls saying that Iblīs made the exception to avoid lying; even Iblīs' avoidance of a lie shows lying's extreme baseness.
rows.anchor: أن لا يصير كاذبا في دعواه فلما احترز إبليس عن الكذب علمنا أن الكذب في غاية الخساسة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Kathīr, Ibn ʿĀmir, and Abū ʿAmr read mukhliṣīn with kasra, meaning people who purify their religion and worship from anything opposing faith and monotheism; the others read mukhlaṣīn with fatḥa.
rows.anchor: قرأ ابن كثير وابن عامر وأبو عمرو : { المخلصين } بكسر اللام في كل القرآن ، والباقون بفتح اللام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With fatḥa, mukhlaṣīn means those whom God has purified through guidance, faith, enabling, and protection; this reading shows that sincerity and faith come only from God.
rows.anchor: ومن فتح اللام فمعناه : الذين أخلصهم الله بالهداية والإيمان ، والتوفيق ، والعصمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sincerity means making something free of another's admixture; acts may be for God alone, another alone, both together, or without any purpose, the last being impossible because action requires motive.
rows.anchor: الإخلاص جعل الشيء خالصا عن شائبة الغير فنقول : كل من أتى بعمل فإما أن يكون قد أتى به لله فقط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An act done solely for God's pleasure is certainly sincere for God, while an act done solely for someone else is not sincere for God.
rows.anchor: وأما الثاني : وهو الإخلاص في حق غير الله ، فظاهر أن هذا لا يكون إخلاصا في حق الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When an act mixes motives but God's pleasure predominates, Rāzī hopes it counts as sincere because the excess over the other motive remains untainted; the remaining categories are not sincere for God.
rows.anchor: أن جانب الله يكون راجحا ، فهذا يرجى أن يكون من المخلصين ، لأن المثل يقابله المثل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Though Iblīs' words seem to claim power over some servants, God says he has no power over any servant, sincere or otherwise; those who follow him choose to do so and are not compelled.
rows.anchor: فبين تعالى في هذه الآية أنه ليس له سلطان على أحد من عبيد الله سواء كانوا مخلصين أو لم يكونوا مخلصين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī links this denial of satanic power to Iblīs' admission that he only called people and they answered, and to the statement that Satan's authority is over his allies and those who associate partners with God.
rows.anchor: ونظير هذه الآية قوله تعالى حكاية عن إبليس أنه قال : { وما كان لى عليكم من سلطان إلا أن دعوتكم فاستجبتم لى }

rows.speaker: الجبائي
rows.claim: Al-Jubbāʾī says the verse refutes popular claims that Satan or jinn can possess people, remove their reason, or do so through sorcery.
rows.anchor: قال الجبائي : هذه الآية تدل على بطلان قول من زعم أن الشيطان والجن يمكنهم صرع الناس وإزالة عقولهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An alternative interpretation is that God confirms Iblīs' claim that he cannot lead the sincere astray, saying he has no authority except over his astray followers.
rows.anchor: وهو أن إبليس لما قال : { إلا عبادك منهم المخلصين } ( الحجر : 40 )

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbī identifies God's servants in this verse as the same servants Iblīs excluded.
rows.anchor: فلهذا قال الكلبي : العباد المذكورون في هذه الآية هم الذين استثناهم إبليس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the first interpretation, illā is a true exception: those who follow the astray are under Iblīs' authority because they obey him in commands and prohibitions.
rows.anchor: على القول الأول يمكن أن يكون قوله : { إلا من اتبعك } استثناء ، لأن المعنى : أن عبادي ليس لك عليهم سلطان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the alternative interpretation, illā cannot be an exception and means “but.” Ibn ʿAbbās says the promised Hell includes Iblīs, his followers, and all who followed the astray.
rows.anchor: وأما على القول الثاني فيمتنع أن يكون استثناء ، بل تكون لفظة ( إلا ) بمعنى لكن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to set out is read with hamza cut or joined, from the verbs asrā and sarā.
rows.anchor: قرىء { فأسر } بقطع الهمزة ووصلها من أسرى وسرى

rows.speaker: صاحب الإقليد
rows.claim: Al-Kashshāf transmits al-Iqlīd's gloss of the night journey as travel in the last part of the night.
rows.anchor: وروى صاحب الكشاف عن صاحب الإقليد فسر { من } السير والقطع آخر الليل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An unattributed poetic line uses qaṭʿ for a stretch of dark night, illustrating the expression for the time of the journey.
rows.anchor: قال الشاعر : افتحي الباب وانظري في النجوم … كم علينا من قطع ليل بهيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Follow their tracks” means follow the traces of Lot's daughters and household.
rows.anchor: وقوله : { واتبع أدبارهم } معناه : اتبع آثار بناتك وأهلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ban on looking back prevents anyone from lagging into the punishment, seeing the devastation, delaying instead of hurrying, or returning for belongings left behind.
rows.anchor: الفائدة فيه أشياء : أحدها : لئلا يتخلف منكم أحد فينا له العذاب

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says “go where you are commanded” means Syria.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس : يعني الشام

rows.speaker: المفضل
rows.claim: Al-Mufaḍḍal says it means the place Gabriel tells them to go; Gabriel directed them to a particular village whose people had not done what Lot's people did.
rows.anchor: قال المفضل : حيث يقول لكم جبريل . وذلك لأن جبريل عليه السلام أمرهم أن يمضوا إلى قرية معينة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qada is construed with ilā because it carries the sense of awḥaynā, “We revealed to him” a decree already made irrevocable; compare 17:4 and 10:71.
rows.anchor: عدى قضينا بإلى ، لأنه ضمن معنى أوحينا ، كأنه قيل : وأوحيناه إليه مقضيا مبتوتا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The decree is first left implicit and then explained as the destruction of Lot's people, a rhetorical sequence that magnifies its gravity.
rows.anchor: وفي إبهامه أولا ، وتفسيره ثانيا تفخيم للأمر وتعظيم له

rows.speaker: الأعمش
rows.claim: Al-Aʿmash reads anna with kasra as a fresh statement, as though someone asked what the decree was and the answer followed.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الأعمش { ءان } بالكسر على الاستئناف كان قائلا قال أخبرنا عن ذلك الأمر

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masʿūd's reading adds “and We said” before the statement that the last remnant of these people would be cut off.
rows.anchor: وفي قراءة ابن مسعود . وقلنا : { أن دابر هؤلآء }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dābir means their last remnant: they would be exterminated to the last person; muṣbiḥīn means when morning appears.
rows.anchor: ودابرهم آخرهم ، يعني يستأصلون عن آخرهم حتى لا يبقى منهم أحد وقوله : { مصبحين } أي حال ظهور الصبح

rows.speaker: أهل المعاني
rows.claim: Ahl al-Maʿānī say the verse does not itself establish that the deadly cry was Gabriel's; that identification needs strong external proof.
rows.anchor: قال أهل المعاني : ليس في الآية دلالة على أن تلك الصيحة صيحة جبريل عليه السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Without strong evidence for Gabriel's role, the verse only shows that a tremendous, deadly cry came upon them.
rows.anchor: وإلا فليس في الآية دلالة إلا على أنه جاءتهم صيحة عظيمة مهلكة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mushriqīn means entering sunrise, the rising of the sun; the root can describe anything that appears from the east.
rows.anchor: يقال شرق الشارق يشرق شروقا لكل ما طلع من جانب الشرق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God punished them in three ways: a terrible cry, overturning the city, and raining down stones of sijjīl; Rāzī says the latter details were explained in Sūrat Hūd.
rows.anchor: عذبهم بثلاثة أنواع من العذاب : أحدها : الصيحة الهائلة المنكرة . وثانيها : أنه جعل عاليها سافلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Exegetes explain mutawassimin as those who discern, look, contemplate, take warning, or see clearly.
rows.anchor: واختلفت عبارات المفسرين في تفسير المتوسمين قيل : المتفرسين ، وقيل : الناظرين

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjāj says the word's linguistic sense is to examine steadily until one recognizes a thing's mark, quality, or sign.
rows.anchor: قال الزجاج : حقيقة المتوسمين في اللغة المتثبتون في نظرهم حتى يعرفوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun in “it is on an enduring road” returns to Lot's city; its visible, undimmed ruins remain on the route from the Ḥijāz to Syria.
rows.anchor: الضمير في قوله : { وإنها } عائد إلى مدينة قوم لوط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Believers know God exacted vengeance on the ignorant for His prophets, while unbelievers attribute the destruction to worldly events, planetary conjunctions, or celestial alignments.
rows.anchor: كل من آمن بالله وصدق الأنبياء والرسل عرف أن ذلك إنما كان لأجل أن الله تعالى انتقم لأنبيائه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After laying out proofs of divine unity, God says He explained them to remove excuses, so people perish or live on the basis of clear proof.
rows.anchor: شرح دلائل التوحيد قال : { وعلى الله قصد السبيل } أي إنما ذكرت هذه الدلائل وشرحتها إزاحة للعذر وإزالة للعلة

rows.speaker: الواحدي
rows.claim: Al-Wāḥidī defines qaṣd as a straight route; a qaṣd or qāṣid road takes a traveler to the desired destination, and the verse elides “clarification of.”
rows.anchor: قال الواحدي : القصد استقامة الطريق يقال : طريق قصد وقاصد إذا أداك إلى مطلوبك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jāʾir means deviating from what is right; the feminine pronoun refers to السبيل, feminine in Hijazi Arabic, and crooked paths are disbelief and misguidance.
rows.anchor: ومعنى الجور في اللغة الميل عن الحق والكناية في قوله : { ومنها جائر } تعود على السبيل

rows.speaker: المعتزلة
rows.claim: The Muʿtazilites infer that God must guide people to true religion and remove excuses because “upon God” indicates obligation, as in the pilgrimage verse; they also infer He does not cause misguidance.
rows.anchor: قالت المعتزلة : دلت الآية على أنه يجب على الله تعالى الإرشاد والهداية إلى الدين وإزاحة العلل والأعذار

rows.speaker: أصحابنا
rows.claim: Rāzī's Ashʿarite side replies that God is obliged by grace and generosity to clarify true religion, but is not obliged to explain how He leads astray.
rows.anchor: أجاب أصحابنا أن المراد على الله بحسب الفضل والكرم أن يبين الدين الحق والمذهب الصحيح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The conditional “if He had willed, He would have guided you all” shows God did not will the unbelievers' guidance or faith, so they were not guided.
rows.anchor: معناه : لو شاء هدايتكم لهداكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This passage begins by naming some of God's blessings created on earth.
rows.anchor: المقصود من هذه الآية ذكر بعض النعم التي خلقها الله تعالى في الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For an tamīda bikum, Kufans understand “so it does not shake,” while Basrans understand “out of dislike that it shake”; mayd is movement and swaying right and left, discussed at 4:176.
rows.anchor: قوله : { أن تميد بكم } يعني لئلا تميد بكم على قول الكوفيين وكراهة أن تميد بكم على قول البصريين

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority compare the earth on water to a boat: it wavered until God set heavy mountains on it like anchors, making it stable.
rows.anchor: المشهور عن الجمهور في تفسير هذه الآية أن قالوا : إن السفينة إذا ألقيت على وجه الماء ، فإنها تميد من جانب إلى جانب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī objects that if earth is naturally heavier than water it would sink rather than float and wobble like a hollow wooden boat; if natures do not cause motion, God's creation of movement and rest makes the mountain explanation fail.
rows.anchor: هذا التعليل مشكل على كل التقديرات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further objection asks what keeps the supporting water in its place: if its nature does so, the same account could explain the earth; if God does, He could directly keep the earth still.
rows.anchor: فما المقتضى لسكون ذلك الماء ووقوفه في حيزه المخصوص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third objection is that movement of the entire enormous earth over the sea would be imperceptible; proponents compare it to a passenger not sensing a moving ship, while Rāzī replies that visible quakes move only a small part.
rows.anchor: أن مجموع الأرض جسم عظيم ، فبتقدير أن تميد كليته وتضطرب على وجه البحر المحيط لم تظهر تلك الحالة للناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāzī's own approach begins from the demonstrable spherical shape of earth and treats its mountains as surface roughnesses.
rows.anchor: ثبت بالدلائل اليقينية أن الأرض كرة ، وثبت أن هذه الجبال على سطح هذه الكرة جارية مجرى خشونات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A smooth sphere would rotate with little cause, while massive mountains directed toward the world's center act like pegs that prevent earth's rotation, wobbling, and movement.
rows.anchor: فكان تخليق هذه الجبال على وجه الأرض كالأوتاد المغروزة في الكرة المانعة لها عن الحركة المستديرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Rivers” is coordinated with mountains; although alqāʾ suggests casting downward, here it means making or creating, as shown by 50:7, 41:10, and “I cast love upon you” at 20:39.
rows.anchor: ألقى ا في الأرض أنهارا كما قال : { وألقينا فيها رواسي }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The expression of casting can approximate bringing down from above, but in these examples it means creation or making rather than literal throwing.
rows.anchor: إلا أن المراد من هذا الإلقاء الجعل والخلق قال تعالى : { وألقيت عليك محبة منى }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rational sciences establish that most rivers rise from springs in mountains, explaining why rivers follow mountains in the verse.
rows.anchor: ثبت في العلوم العقلية أن أكثر الأنهار إنما تتفجر منابعها في الجبال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Paths are also coordinated with mountains: God laid them out so travelers could find their way, as in 20:53; “so that you may be guided” states their purpose.
rows.anchor: وهي أيضا على قوله : { وألقى فى الارض رواسى } والتقدير : وألقى في الأرض سبلا ومعناه : أنه تعالى أظهرها وبينها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Signs are coordinated with mountains, rivers, and paths and mean route markers; these include mountains and winds, and some people identify roads by smelling soil.
rows.anchor: والمراد بالعلامات معالم الطرق وهي الأشياء التي بها يهتدي

rows.speaker: الأخفش
rows.claim: Al-Akhfash says the sentence ends at “signs,” and “by the star they are guided” begins a separate statement; star is then a generic singular.
rows.anchor: قال الأخفش تم الكلام عند قوله : { وعلامات } وقوله : { وبالنجم هم يهتدون } كلام منفصل

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddī identifies the stars as the Pleiades, the two al-Farqadān, Banāt Naʿsh, and al-Jady.
rows.anchor: وعن السدي هو الثريا ، والفرقدان ، وبنات نعش ، والجدي

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan reads nجم as a plural in two vocalizations, nujum and nujm; the second is a lightened form.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الحسن : { وبالنجم } بضمتين وبضمة فسكون ، وهو جمع نجم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation says the wāw was omitted from the word star for ease of pronunciation.
rows.anchor: وقيل : حذف الواو من النجم تخفيفا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The address shifts from present listeners about earth's shaking to absent “they” because Quraysh frequently traveled for trade and therefore knew the benefits of star navigation especially well.
rows.anchor: إن قريشا كانت تكثر أسفارها لطلب المال ، ومن كثرت أسفاره كان علمه بالمنافع الحاصلة من الاهتداء بالنجوم أكثر وأتم
